title: Senator-judges ask why defense witness weighing in on report he hasn't read
summary: Senator-judges cast doubt on the capability of a defense witness to answer questions about a report detailing Duterte"s alleged unexplained wealth, especially since he didn't read it.

blocks.text: Senator-judges cast doubt on the capability of a defense witness to answer questions about a report detailing Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth, especially after it was revealed that he did not read the report at all.

At Duterte's impeachment trial on Thursday, defense counsel Mark Vinluan presented AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Consulting PH head Rainer Dela Fuente, asking him about the findings of prosecution witness Alexander Cabrera.
Cabrera, a financial forensic analyst, presented a report alleging that Duterte had unexplained wealth amounting to at least P817 million.
Much of Vinluan’s questioning referred to Cabrera’s report, repeatedly calling Cabrera a “so-called expert.”
“In financial investigations, how important is it to meticulously go through the records one by one, instead of considering summaries based on mere conjectures?” Vinuluan.
Dela Fuente said that it was very important, saying that deviations could cast doubt on computations.
“We cannot base, especially if it concerns financial investigations, it is not just based on conductures, There should be facts,” Dela Fuente said in a mix of English and Filipino.
However, Vinluan’s line of questioning also strayed to other matters.
In one instance, Vinluan showed Dela Fuente a photo of a P13.5 million Benz G-Wagon and asked him what he thought of a politician who owned such a car.
“I’d rather not answer that,” Dela Fuente said.

A few questions later, Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo spoke up, asking Senate Impeachment presiding officer Francis Escudero to put the witness on a shorter leash and asking about his qualifications to testify on the matter.

Senator-judge Joel Villanueva also raised that Dela Fuente's subpoena only asked that he was there for his expertise in AML and related matters. He asked Escudero if Dela Fuente was there to refute Cabrera’s report.
“Did you give the witness a copy of the forensic report?” Villanueva asked Vinluan.
“No, Your Honor,” Vinluan replied. He further justified that the defense did not want to have prior correspondence with the defense witness.
“If he is to refute the report then he should have seen the report,” Villanueva said.
Tulfo echoed Villanueva’s sentiment.
“In the first place, wala siyang ideya kung ano yung nakasaad sa sinabi ng testigo… dapat beforehand, he was given a copy of those documents para mapag-aralan niya,” Tulfo said.
(In the first place, he does not have an idea on what is said by the witness… it should have been beforehand, he was given a copy of those documents so he could study it.)
Tulfo asked why even the ownership of a G-Wagon was raised.
“Ano ito, salesman na rin?” he added.
(What is he? A salesman?)
Senator-judge Bam Aquino also questioned Dela Fuente, asking if none of the financial and bank records subpoenaed by the impeachment court was shown to him.
Dela Fuente could be heard off-camera saying “none.”

“It’s really concepts and general ideas about AMLA [AML Act] and financial investigations? Okay, Mr. Witness, and again, hindi mo ito kasalanan, but many times we have witnesses here, pag tinatanong namin, ang sinasagot namin, ‘Hindi ho namin alam’. So gusto amin ng mga witness na pwede kami sagutin dirtso talaga,” Aquino said.
(This is not your fault, but many times we've had witnesses here, and when we ask them questions, they reply 'We don't know.' So we want a witness who can give us direct answers.)
During Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros’ interjection, Dela Fuente said that he still respected Cabrera but maintained that the law should be followed.

“Ang ginagawa ko lang ho, binabangga ang kanyang ginawa sa kung ano yung mayroon sa batas. Kung ito po ay maga-align, yun ang aking role dito… I don’t need to read the full report going here because kahit i-flash yan ngayon palang, makikita niyo na po, aligned ba ito sa provisions ng AMLA?” Dela Fuente said.

(What I did here was compare what he did on what is in the law, if this was aligned, that is what my role is… I don’t need to read the full report going here because even if it is flashed just now, you can see it now, is it aligned with AMLA?) — BM, GMA News
